_comment_format: Fitch contract structure, revision r2. 5 roles run in sequence; each reads the contract and adds its own section OR explicitly writes not_applicable with a reason. This is the input for the FITCH-PLAN.md/PLAN.md synthesis. Style is INLINE-BODIES: real content lives in the fields (description carries the actual spec, wave_gate carries a concrete DoD command) — not a placeholder like 'one-paragraph spec' left unfilled.
_comment_usage: Built by the CC orchestrator during fitch (PIPELINE.md §5): analyst -> designer -> tech_lead -> toster -> devops, one autonomous pass. Self-audit A-G (a fresh adversarial subagent, pre-W1, PIPELINE.md §6) is folded back in -> contract_revision becomes r2, with audit_findings_addressed listing what was folded.
_comment_r2_distinctive: Mandatory r2-distinctive fields (the housekeeping gate checks THESE, not a bare not_applicable): contract_revision (top level) + audit_findings_addressed (in summary). If the epic ran without a self-audit A-G, contract_revision = 'r1 (no self-audit)' and audit_findings_addressed = [] with an explicit note — do not delete the fields.
installer_slot: <slot prefix> <version> | none - docs/chore, no version bump
fitch_audit: <.claude/fitch/<slug>/self-audit-A-G.md (X HIGH + Y MED folded into r2) | n/a (r1)>

analyst.key_finding: <one-line summary of what the analyst found in the code/docs>

requirements.title: <title>
requirements.description: <INLINE BODY: a real specification - which files/functions/lines, what changes and why, the audit-finding id if folded. Not a placeholder like 'one-paragraph spec' - concrete, grounded in disk.>

designer.not_applicable_reason: <if the epic has no UI, e.g. 'No UI in this epic - process documents only'>
designer.design_tokens: <reference to the design system file, or 'use existing'>

tech_lead.key_finding: <INLINE: N waves, who executes them (CC orchestrator + subagents autonomously per ORCHESTRATOR.md, or tech-lead authors directly for a docs epic), file-isolation = 1 owner per file>

waves.name: <wave name>
waves.wave_gate: <INLINE: a CONCRETE DoD command + expected metric. E.g.: grep -cE '^## #[0-7]' file == 8 ; test -f X ; grep -c 'marker' Y >= N. Not a placeholder like 'concrete DoD command'.>

conflicts_resolved.issue: touched by W2 task-X and W4 task-Y
conflicts_resolved.resolution: sequential - no race | PASTE-FIRST: T05 archive-landing BEFORE T04's cut

toster.key_finding: <INLINE: what DoD means here (passing spec / doc-invariant greps against REAL lines / git+baseline) + who runs the pre-merge manual smoke and on what>

qa_matrix.test_type: unit | E2E spec | grep | bash | manual smoke
qa_matrix.verification_command: <INLINE concrete bash: grep -c / test -f / npm run test -- --spec ... | grep passing>

weak_assertions.issue: <negative-only assertion / gate the meaning, not the literal string>
weak_assertions.fix: <concrete suggestion - a positive assertion plus a manual spot-check pre-merge>

devops.not_applicable_reason: <if docs/chore: 'No product version bump/installer; close = audit baseline +-0 + push (loose-ref verified) + NO tag'>

installer.build_command: <wrapper script - the project's release/build-installer entry point>

devops.rollback_plan: <brief - git revert the merge commit, mark the previous installer as latest>

key_risks: <risk 1 - e.g. a lesson: gate on REAL lines, not absent ones (false-green is caught by a positive assertion)>
<risk 2 - a ZERO-LOSS / sacred-invariant that must not be violated>

audit_findings_addressed.finding: <letter+number from self-audit A-G, e.g. E1 / B2>
audit_findings_addressed.fix_in_task: <T<NN> / QA<NN> / R<NN> where it was closed>
